summary_en: This study tests acalabrutinib, obinutuzumab, and glofitamab given together for mantle cell lymphoma that has come back after a period of improvement or did not respond to earlier treatment. Acalabrutinib is taken by mouth twice a day, obinutuzumab and glofitamab are given through a vein, and treatment repeats every 21 days for up to 12 cycles unless the disease progresses or side effects are unacceptable. The record does not state a main outcome; it is a phase 2 study of side effects and how well the drugs work together.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa acalabrutinib, obinutuzumab y glofitamab administrados juntos para el linfoma de células del manto que regresó después de un periodo de mejoría o que no respondió a tratamientos previos. El acalabrutinib se toma por vía oral dos veces al día, mientras que el obinutuzumab y el glofitamab se administran por vena, y el tratamiento se repite cada 21 días hasta por 12 ciclos, salvo que la enfermedad progrese o los efectos secundarios sean inaceptables. El registro no indica un resultado principal; es un estudio de fase 2 sobre los efectos secundarios y qué tan bien funcionan los medicamentos juntos.
who_for: Mantle cell lymphoma that has come back or did not respond after at least one prior systemic therapy
Tumor that is CD20-positive after the most recent therapy
Disease that is measurable on imaging under Lugano criteria
ECOG performance status of 2 or lower, with blood counts and organ function in set ranges
not_for: Prior treatment with a T-cell engaging bispecific antibody
More than 180 cumulative days of prior BTK inhibitor use without progression
CAR T cell therapy within 6 months before starting study treatment
Prior allogeneic stem cell transplant or autologous transplant within 3 months
Known active lymphoma involving the central nervous system
